summary: Named on an Ontario still-standing list; the MNR removed the bottom ladder section and asks visitors not to climb; no source found on the site today.

access.note: The list says the MNR removed the bottom 20 ft of ladder and asks visitors not to climb. It does not say whether the site is open to the public.

facts.status_note: Listed as still standing on an Ontario list kept unchanged after 2013. The MNR decided in 2013 to remove many such towers; no source confirms this one stands today.

evidence.supports: Tower listed at Humbolt Bay, Lake Nipigon
evidence.quote: 10- Iron Range Bluff Tower- Humbolt Bay, Lake Nipigon, Ont.

evidence.supports: Canada Lookouts Ontario index gives the same location
The Ontario MNR decided as of 2013 to remove many still-standing towers
evidence.quote: The Ontario MNR has decided, as of 2013, to remove many of these still standing towers.

evidence.supports: The list's author said the list would stay as it was
evidence.quote: I will be keeping this list as it is though.

evidence.supports: MNR removed the bottom 20 ft of ladder; climbing is hazardous
evidence.quote: It is hazardous to try to climb one and that is why the MNR has removed the bottom 20 ft of ladder.

evidence.supports: MNR no longer maintains the towers; visitors asked not to climb
evidence.quote: The MNR no longer maintains them so please refrain from climbing.

notes_for_editor: Only two list pages support this story. Neither gives a build year, height, design or staffing history, so the story is short. The list was kept unchanged after the 2013 MNR decision, so its still-standing label is not a current check. Both sources spell the bay 'Humbolt'; 'Humboldt' may be intended, which I could not confirm. The brief's agency line (Department of Lands and Forests, to 1972) is not in the two pages read, so it is replaced by the MNR named in the list. The access level 'restricted' reflects the ladder removal and climbing request only; the source does not say whether the site is open. One WebSearch found nothing tower-specific. Suggested checks: Ontario MNR tower decommissioning records, Thunder Bay archives. Fact-check 2026-10-20: the lead now says the tower is 'listed as' an Ontario fire tower rather than 'is' one, because no source read confirms it stands today; the author and MNR sentences were reworded to avoid copying quote wording.
